name: search_memory
description: Search all current long-term memory by default, including global user decisions. A task about a named project still uses scope=all; do not infer a project filter from the task or workspace. Use scope=project only when the user explicitly asks to exclude other projects' memory. Reuse a returned fact for every question it already answers; searching its other keywords does not independently verify it. Search again for a still-unanswered question or new conflict, and check current applicability against the relevant sources. Use focused topic keywords rather than a list of every file, tool and task detail. The output contains readable titles and whole statements. Large results include a continuation call; follow it to read the rest. Empty queries browse current knowledge with natural modules. A long entry may first return its title and a detail=full call for its complete text. Use search_raw when exact conversation evidence is needed.

project_name.description: Optional task context, ignored as a filter with scope=all. Required only for a user-requested project-only filter; relevant decisions may be stored under global or other labels.

query.description: The specific topic or missing decision to recover; avoid concatenating unrelated task keywords.

budget_tokens.description: Size of the complete returned page, using cl100k_base when available or conservative UTF-8 byte counting. Omit to use cost_budget.search_tokens.

cursor.description: Reading position from the returned continuation call; the Agent follows it automatically.

detail.description: auto returns whole facts fitting the page. full explicitly reads one complete entry, even when it exceeds the page size.

scope.description: Keep all for ordinary tasks, even tasks about one project. project excludes global and other labels: use only when the user explicitly requests that restriction.
